Keep September (P): at this run's provider routing both candidates cost 27–28% more per reply, and neither keeps Kairo in character better, so cost decides.

Both candidates stay inside the declared 15-point margin on the character pass rate, so the keep rests on cost. A candidate priced below September (P) under another provider routing would win, and the routing behind these costs is not recorded.

!
Confidence: High, if the caveats below aren't material.
  • Provider routing not recorded. Material if a candidate served under another routing costs less than September (P)'s $1.89 per 1,000 replies: under the declared margin it would then be the pick. The high applies to the cost order at this run's routing, which already contradicts an earlier finding that qwen3.8-flash (A) lowers production cost.
  • The judge is not calibrated. Only if the judge marks the candidates' style down unfairly; the pass-rate verdicts already let both candidates through the margin, so a misreading would change how far behind they are, not the keep, which rests on cost at this routing.
  • The aspect was set after the results. Only if a different aspect, chosen before the results, would show a candidate ahead of September (P) by enough to pay for its higher cost.
  • The control was set after the results. Only if another arm should have been the baseline; the cost gaps and pass rates do not depend on which arm is called the control.
  • A confound: model. Only if a lever other than the model moved between arms along with it; each arm's recorded settings name the model alone.
  • The margin was set after the results. The late margin was checked: the call holds at every margin.
  • The floor was set after the results. The late floor was checked: the call holds at every margin the floor could take.
RecommendationKeep September (P) (the control). At this run's routing it is the cheapest arm at $1.89 per 1,000 replies, and neither candidate is ahead of it on character.
Why not the othersqwen3.8-flash (A): costs $0.62 per 1,000 replies more at this routing. Its pass rate is 7.6 points lower, clearly worse in size (-10.8 to -3.4 points) but inside the margin, so cost, not character, rules it out.
Why not the others1017 (B): costs $0.49 per 1,000 replies more at this routing, for a pass rate not told apart from September (P)'s (-5.8 to +1.1 points); the judge also puts it 4.7 points behind on persona holds character.

This run contradicts the earlier finding that qwen3.8-flash (A) lowers production cost: here it costs 28% more, at a routing the snapshot does not record. If that finding holds under another routing, qwen3.8-flash (A) becomes the pick under today's margin despite its clear drop.

At this run's unrecorded provider routing, both candidates cost more per reply than September (P): qwen3.8-flash (A) by $0.62 per 1,000 replies and 1017 (B) by $0.49 per 1,000 replies, each interval clear of zero, and the order holds even with September (P)'s unreported trials filled at its own p95 and the candidates' at zero.

Production cost, per 1,000 replies, in dollars.

Paired production-cost gap against September (P), corrected intervals, over trials where both arms reported cost; each arm's mean in the options summary (28% and 27% above September (P)) is read over that arm's own reported trials, so the two do not match exactly. The paired intervals may be too narrow if they count trials nested in conversations. Unreported cost: 33 trials for September (P), 69 for qwen3.8-flash (A), 18 for 1017 (B); September (P) at $2.02 per 1,000 replies with each at its own p95 still undercuts qwen3.8-flash (A) at $2.24 per 1,000 replies and 1017 (B) at $2.36 per 1,000 replies with each free. 1017 (B) spent 55% of its output reasoning against 76% for September (P), so part of its gap may belong to reasoning, not the model.

Neither candidate keeps Kairo in character better, and both stay inside the 15-point margin: qwen3.8-flash (A) passes 7.6 points less often than September (P), clearly worse but allowed, and 1017 (B) is 3 points down, not told apart from it.

Caveats: A run fell short of its usable measurements — two of them, on qwen3.8-flash (A); A confound: reasoning ratio.

Change in the character pass rate against September (P), with the declared margin. qwen3.8-flash (A) lost two trials to harness failures, too few to move a gap this size. 1017 (B)'s different reasoning share could move its reading either way.

Off lane, the gap to September (P) reads -40.5 to -5.3 points for qwen3.8-flash (A) and -37.4 to -2.9 for 1017 (B); these intervals are unpaired and uncorrected, and may be too narrow because repeats of one case are not independent.

All three models slip on off-lane asks, each its own way: the 1017 (B) card narrates the listener in the third person, the qwen3.8-flash (A) card does the out-of-lane task it was asked, and the September (P) card falls into a customer-service refusal.

One kept off-lane failure per arm, of 39 for September (P), 64 for qwen3.8-flash (A) and 62 for 1017 (B); they show the kinds of slip, not their shares.

Next steps

  • The persona owner declares whether the 15-point margin on the character pass rate stands for the next round. Whether a cheaper qwen3.8-flash (A) would be acceptable despite its clear drop; today's margin lets it through, a margin under 10.8 points would not.
  • Re-price qwen3.8-flash (A) and 1017 (B) with each arm's provider routing recorded, and reconcile with the earlier round's cost finding. Whether the cost uplift belongs to the routing or the models; a candidate cheaper than September (P) under the declared margin would become the pick.
  • Calibrate the judge against human ratings of character, drawing heavily on off-lane conversations. Whether the persona holds character gaps and the off-lane weakness are real or the judge's taste; it turns the judge caveat into evidence either way.
  • Write an off-lane directive for September (P) and rerun the off-lane stratum. Whether the large stratum where every model loses most can lift on the model being kept.
  • Only if 1017 (B) stays of interest: rerun it at a reasoning share matched to September (P)'s with 815 cases per arm. Whether its pass-rate drop of 3 points is real and belongs to the model, four times in five.

Left out, and why

The delivery check (a Discord message or queued voice sent) and failed-reply notices
Neither candidate is separated from the control on either, so they do not bear on the keep.
The ordinal outcome and transcript judged scores
Further views of the same conversations from the same uncalibrated judge: qwen3.8-flash (A) is lower on both, 1017 (B) is not separated on either, which changes nothing in the call.
Measuring spend, all roles
The cost of running the evaluation itself, not of serving Kairo; production cost is the serving cost the call weighs.
Strata smaller than the six shown (emotional, lineage, next up, assistant shape and the rest)
Too few cases each to read; their gaps carry intervals that cross zero. The full tables hold them.
Per-stratum gap bars with intervals for each candidate
The strata table carries the rates the claim turns on, and the off-lane intervals are stated in its caption; the other strata's gaps cross zero.
Items delivered, tool provider faults and turns that ran over budget
Describe the run's mechanics and do not bear on the call.
Latency
Read while other runs executed beside it, so it is not comparable between arms.

Method

Cases and repeats
299 conversations, each run 3 times per arm on the character adherence (v2) aspect, run on 2026-10-25.
What pass means
A trial passes the character check as the campaign scored it; the snapshot names no grader for the aspect, so what makes a pass is not stated beyond its count of trials passed over usable.
Intervals
Readings against the control, and the margin test, are at 95%. Contrasts are paired and corrected together by Holm's method over a family of 16, each at 99.69%. Strata gaps are unpaired and uncorrected; where trials nest within conversations some intervals may be too narrow.
Judge
Judged dimensions are scored by openai/gpt-6-luna, uncalibrated, with 0 human ratings.
Cost basis
Production cost per 1,000 replies, as each arm was served in this run; no provider is recorded for any arm and no monthly volume is declared, so no monthly figure is stated. Arm means are read over each arm's reported trials; the gaps are paired contrasts.
Late declarations
The aspect, control, margin and floor were all set on 25 Oct 2026, after the results.
Simulator
The simulated user's request settings were not recorded on every run, so whether they varied cannot be established.

Caveats: The apparatus may have differed: simulator sent settings.

Not compared
Latency was read under concurrent execution and is left out; input tokens, output tokens and model-call counts were not reported.

Caveats: Latency is not compared; Recorded but not reported: input tokens; Recorded but not reported: output tokens; Recorded but not reported: llm calls.

Source
The frozen campaign snapshot for Kairo persona round two.
